32 Which component has the I–V graph shown?
I
V
0
0
A
filament lamp
B
metallic conductor at constant temperature
C
resistor of fixed resistance
D
semiconductor diode

hints: Notice the shape of the $I$ against $V$ curve from the origin: it starts steep and then bends over so its gradient decreases as $V$ increases.
Recall that gradient of an $I$-$V$ graph is $1/R$, so a decreasing gradient means resistance $R = V/I$ is increasing with current.
Think about which listed component heats up significantly when current flows and therefore has increasing resistance, compared with ohmic conductors and a one-way diode.
walkthrough: Look at the axes: current $I$ is plotted vertically against potential difference $V$ horizontally, starting at the origin in the first quadrant.
Recall that for any point, resistance is $R = V/I$, and the small-signal gradient is $dI/dV = 1/R$. A straight line through the origin means constant $R$.
Here the curve bends toward the $V$-axis, so for equal extra $V$ you get less extra $I$. The gradient $dI/dV$ decreases, so $R$ increases as $V$ and $I$ increase.
Link this to heating: larger $I$ dissipates more power $P = IV$ in the component, raising its temperature and increasing lattice vibrations that scatter electrons.
A filament lamp shows exactly this effect because its thin wire gets very hot and its resistance rises markedly, while a constant-temperature metal or fixed resistor stays ohmic with a straight line.
A semiconductor diode is different again because it conducts essentially in one direction with a sharp turn-on, not a smooth curve flattening in this way.
The component whose resistance increases with temperature and gives this flattening $I$-$V$ curve is the filament lamp. This is option A

A.explanation: Filament heats up as $V$ and $I$ increase, so resistance $R = V/I$ increases and the $I$-$V$ curve flattens toward the $V$-axis as shown.

B.explanation: A metallic conductor at constant temperature is ohmic, so its $I$-$V$ graph is a straight line through the origin, not a curve that flattens.

C.explanation: A resistor of fixed resistance obeys $I = V/R$, so its $I$-$V$ graph is a straight line of constant gradient $1/R$.

D.explanation: A semiconductor diode passes current freely in forward bias only after a threshold and blocks reverse current, giving a very asymmetric characteristic, not this gradual flattening from the origin.
